newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan pension fund body suspends deals with DKB.
newsitem.headline: Japan pension fund body suspends deals with DKB.

text.p: Japan's Pension Welfare Service Public Corp (PWSPC), an affiliate of the Health Ministry, said on Tuesday it had temporarily suspended its pension fund management dealings with Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB).

"We are temporarily suspending deals with DKB due to its recent scandal. We plan to take formal (punitive) measures when supervising authorities punitively take administrative steps," said an official of the PWSPC.
Top executives of DKB resigned on Friday and the bank admitted it had been unable to cut its ties to racketeers in a widening saga of dubious deals and illegal payoffs.
DKB said the bank had made a total of 26 billion yen in loans to Yoshinori Koike, the younger brother of Ryuichi Koike, the racketeer at the heart of the Nomura Securities payoff scandal.
The PWSPC manages about 24 trillion yen worth of funds in the financial markets, he said.
Ninety percent of the funds is entrusted to trust banks and life insurance companies, he said.
The pension fund body itself manages the remainder mostly with the assistance of investment advisory companies.
DKB manages funds on behalf of the PWSPC in such short-term instruments as certificates of deposit.
